newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Singapore, Manchester voted best world airports.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Manchester voted best world airports.

text.p: Singapore's Changi and Britain's Manchester have been voted the world's top two airports by long-haul airline passengers, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said on Wednesday.

But they are closely challenged by Melbourne, which has surged up the table from seventh to third place last year, Amsterdam which slipped from third to fourth place, and by Zurich which emerged fifth in the poll.

The findings -- in which Changi's spanking terminal ousted Manchester, undergoing major reconstruction, from the top spot it held last year -- were based on the views of some 55,000 people and covered 54 airports, IATA said.
Changi, a major transit hub for flights from Europe to Asia and Australasia, was in second place in the 1996 survey.

IATA said Manchester's strong position despite building work could reflect the attitude of the airport's staff who came top of a separate section of the survey for courtesy and friendliness to travellers.

A strong performer included for the first time was Zurich, home base for the Swiss airline Swissair and increasingly a major hub for traffic into the old Soviet Union and beyond, as well as for Africa and Latin America.
The Swiss financial centre's Kloten airport was voted second best after Changi among business passengers, although it emerged as only ninth among leisure travellers.

IATA said the strong showing of Changi, top among both business and leisure passengers, and Amsterdam's Schiphol, fourth for both, demonstrated that large and busy airports were not necessarily low on passenger satisfaction.

"It is clear that with the appropriate customer focus and an ability and willingness to invest in supporting it on an ongoing basis, reasonably large airports can perform strongly," a commentary in IATA's journal Airlines International said.

Australia's Melbourne moved up the table after improving facilities at its international terminal, according to the survey. All travellers voted it top for eating facilities, with Sydney in second place.

In the survey, passengers are asked to rate from one to 10 the airports where they boarded and left their main long-haul flight on a total of 23 service elements ranging from signposting the sense of security.

Athens, bottom of the poll last year and for years target of fierce criticism in the travel industry, was voted the most improved airport of the year, although there has been little infrastructure change at its ageing terminal.

Changi, with its huge array of boutiques catering for a wide variety of customers, came top of the poll for shopping facilities, followed by Schiphol, famed for its duty-free offers, and by Britain's Gatwick.

Gatwick, which came 12th in the overall rating, came top for special services for overseas visitors ahead of Changi, Schiphol and Kloten, second for staff courtesy, and equal second with Kloten for efficiency of check-in staff.

Best overall performing U.S. airport was Cincinatti, sixth in the overall poll for passenger convenience on the strength of friendliness of airport staff, restaurant facilities and efficiency of check-in.
Close behind in seventh place was Florida's Orlando, whose staff came top for both checkin-in courtesy and efficiency, followed by Montreal's Mirabel airport, Sydney and Calgary in 10th place.
